pages.quiz:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does the Arabic word مَا اسْمُكَ؟ (maa ismuka?) mean? (1 mark)
   A. good evening
   B. hello
   C. What is your name? (to a boy)
   D. and upon you peace (the reply)

2. How is the Arabic word مَا اسْمُكَ؟ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. as-salaamu ʿalaykum
   B. shukran
   C. ahlan wa sahlan
   D. maa ismuka?

3. What does the Arabic word عَمٌّ (ʿamm) mean? (1 mark)
   A. father's brother
   B. grandmother
   C. mother's brother
   D. father's sister

4. Which Arabic sentence means "Who is this? (a boy or man)" (1 mark)
   A. هَذِهِ أُمِّي
   B. عِنْدِي أَخٌ وَأُخْتٌ
   C. هَذَا أَبِي
   D. مَنْ هَذَا؟

5. What does the Arabic sentence الْمِصْبَاحُ فَوْقَ الطَّاوِلَةِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The cat is under the bed.
   B. The pen is in the bag.
   C. The book is on the table.
   D. The lamp is above the table.

6. What does the Arabic word ayna ask? (1 mark)
   A. Who
   B. What
   C. Why
   D. Where

7. The cat is under the bed. Which position word is used? (1 mark)
   A. taHta
   B. ʿalaa
   C. fawqa
   D. fii

8. Which sound is in the name of the day al-khamiis? (1 mark)
   A. a soft s only
   B. a hard k
   C. kh, a throat sound
   D. a heavy d

9. What does the Arabic sentence هَلْ عِنْدَكَ حَفْلَةٌ؟ mean? (1 mark)
   A. Blessed festival (Happy Eid).
   B. Happy birthday.
   C. Do you have a party? (to a boy)
   D. May you be well every year.

10. What does the Arabic word تَفَضَّلْ (tafaddal) mean? (1 mark)
   A. juice
   B. gift
   C. please, go ahead
   D. drink

11. Which Arabic word means "stand up"? (1 mark)
   A. أَغْلِقِ الْبَابَ
   B. اِسْمَعْ
   C. قِفْ
   D. اِقْرَأْ

12. Which sentence says 'I hear with my ear'? (1 mark)
   A. aktubu bi-yadii
   B. araa biʿaynii
   C. ashummu bi-anfii
   D. asmaʿu bi-udhunii

13. Which Arabic sentence means "We look after the environment." (1 mark)
   A. الْجَوُّ بَارِدٌ
   B. الْجَوُّ حَارٌّ
   C. نُحَافِظُ عَلَى الْبِيئَةِ
   D. الْجَوُّ مُمْطِرٌ

14. How is the Arabic word سَمَاءٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. ghaa'im
   B. mumtir
   C. samaa'
   D. matar

15. How is the syllable بِي read? (1 mark)
   A. bii
   B. buu
   C. bay
   D. bi

16. How do you read the syllable نِ? (1 mark)
   A. ni
   B. la
   C. buu
   D. muu

17. What is the name of the Arabic letter ت? (1 mark)
   A. Saad
   B. Haa
   C. daal
   D. taa

18. How is the Arabic word أَخٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. usra
   B. khaal
   C. akh
   D. ʿamma

19. How do you read the syllable لَا? (1 mark)
   A. bii
   B. du
   C. si
   D. laa

20. Which day name comes from the Arabic word for 'one'? (1 mark)
   A. as-sabt
   B. al-jumuʿa
   C. al-khamiis
   D. al-ahad

21. What is meant by reading pace? (1 mark)
   A. How many books you read
   B. How tidy your writing is
   C. How loud you read
   D. How fast or slow you read

22. Which Arabic word means "dance"? (1 mark)
   A. حَفْلَةٌ
   B. رَقْصٌ
   C. كَعْكَةٌ
   D. هَدِيَّةٌ

23. How is the Arabic word هَدِيَّةٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. hadiyya
   B. raqs
   C. ʿiid miilaad
   D. sadiiq

24. Which Arabic word means "oranges"? (1 mark)
   A. بُرْتُقَالٌ
   B. طَمَاطِمُ
   C. سَمَكٌ
   D. بَطَاطِسُ

25. Which Arabic word means "vegetables"? (1 mark)
   A. حَلِيبٌ
   B. لَحْمٌ
   C. خُضَارٌ
   D. مَوْزٌ

26. Which of these Arabic words (in English letters) means 'clouds'? (1 mark)
   A. ghaym
   B. riih
   C. matar
   D. shams

27. Which Arabic sentence means "The chair is at the door." (1 mark)
   A. لَا تَلْعَبْ بِالسِّكِّينِ
   B. الْمِفْتَاحُ فِي الْخِزَانَةِ
   C. أُنَظِّفُ أَسْنَانِي
   D. الْكُرْسِيُّ عِنْدَ الْبَابِ

28. Which sound does the Arabic letter ج make? (1 mark)
   A. s as in sun
   B. j as in jug
   C. a quick rolled r
   D. f as in fan

29. Which Arabic word means "mother's brother"? (1 mark)
   A. خَالٌ
   B. ابْنٌ
   C. أُخْتٌ
   D. أَخٌ

30. Which family word is written أُخْتٌ? (1 mark)
   A. umm (mother)
   B. akh (brother)
   C. ukht (sister)
   D. ab (father)

31. What does legible mean? (1 mark)
   A. Very fast
   B. Written in colour
   C. Easy to read
   D. Very small

32. How is the Arabic word لَذِيذٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. ladhiidh
   B. taawila
   C. as-salaamu ʿalaykum
   D. baarid

33. Which of these is a masculine noun? (1 mark)
   A. taawila (table)
   B. kursii (chair)
   C. qitta (cat)
   D. naafidha (window)

34. Why do people use pictures to communicate? (1 mark)
   A. Pictures are always words
   B. Pictures have no meaning
   C. Pictures are only for children
   D. Pictures can be understood by people who speak different languages

35. Which Arabic word means "drink"? (1 mark)
   A. شَمْعَةٌ
   B. عِيدُ مِيلَادٍ
   C. شَرَابٌ
   D. صَدِيقٌ

36. What does nahnu narqusu mean? (1 mark)
   A. We dance.
   B. My mother cooks.
   C. I have a gift.
   D. I like the party.

37. Which style is old, angular and has straight lines? (1 mark)
   A. Naskh
   B. Diwani
   C. Ruqʿah
   D. Kufic

38. What should you write on the back of a body flashcard? (1 mark)
   A. Only your name
   B. The sound and the meaning
   C. A long story
   D. Nothing

39. Which Arabic word means "clean"? (1 mark)
   A. غَائِمٌ
   B. شَجَرَةٌ
   C. نَظِيفٌ
   D. زَهْرَةٌ

40. Which Arabic word means "at (near, by)"? (1 mark)
   A. تَحْتَ
   B. عَلَى
   C. أَمَامَ
   D. عِنْدَ

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Translate into English: al-yawmu yawmu l-khamiis (2 marks)

42. Describe how a group can stage a poem at an interclass festival. (4 marks) (4 marks)

43. Name three rooms of the house in Arabic (English letters) with meanings. (3 marks) (3 marks)

44. List the members of the nuclear family in Arabic (English letters) with their meanings. Give at least four. (4 marks) (4 marks)

45. Translate into English: al-ʿasiiru baarid (2 marks)

46. Translate into English: unadhdhifu asnaanii (2 marks)

47. State the job of each part of a speech: opening, middle and closing. (3 marks) (3 marks)

48. Look at a picture of a birthday party with a cake with a candle and friends standing round the table. Make a prediction and give a reason. (2 marks) (2 marks)

49. Describe two things you can do to pronounce the days of the week correctly. (2 marks) (2 marks)

50. Give three rules for a handwriting contest. (3 marks) (3 marks)

51. Translate into English: yadii Sagiira (2 marks)

52. Explain why we should show respect when we greet people of a different gender or culture. (3 marks) (3 marks)

53. Explain why you should copy sounds carefully when learning Arabic words. (2 marks) (2 marks)

54. Give three things you can do to listen attentively. (3 marks) (3 marks)

55. Translate into English: haadhihi ghurfatii (2 marks)

56. Describe how to draw and label a household item. (4 marks) (4 marks)

57. Translate into English: uhibbu T-taʿaam (2 marks)

58. Explain how drawing and labelling help you to remember new words. (2 marks) (2 marks)

59. Translate into English: aakulu l-aruzza (2 marks)

60. Read these words and write their sounds in English letters with meanings: مَرْحَبًا and شُكْرًا. (4 marks) (4 marks)

61. Write four weather features in Arabic sounds with meanings. (4 marks) (4 marks)

62. Describe how you can make flashcards for the days of the week. (3 marks) (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — What is your name? (to a boy)
   مَا اسْمُكَ؟ (maa ismuka?) means What is your name? (to a boy).

2. D — maa ismuka?
   مَا اسْمُكَ؟ is read maa ismuka? and means What is your name? (to a boy).

3. A — father's brother
   عَمٌّ (ʿamm) means father's brother.

4. D — مَنْ هَذَا؟
   مَنْ هَذَا؟ (man haadhaa?) means: Who is this? (a boy or man)

5. D — The lamp is above the table.
   الْمِصْبَاحُ فَوْقَ الطَّاوِلَةِ (al-misbaahu fawqa t-taawila) means: The lamp is above the table.

6. D — Where
   ayna means 'where'.

7. A — taHta
   taHta means under.

8. C — kh, a throat sound
   The letter kh is a throat sound like a soft clearing of the throat.

9. C — Do you have a party? (to a boy)
   هَلْ عِنْدَكَ حَفْلَةٌ؟ (hal ʿindaka hafla?) means: Do you have a party? (to a boy)

10. C — please, go ahead
   تَفَضَّلْ (tafaddal) means please, go ahead.

11. C — قِفْ
   قِفْ (qif) means stand up.

12. D — asmaʿu bi-udhunii
   asmaʿu means I hear and udhun means ear.

13. C — نُحَافِظُ عَلَى الْبِيئَةِ
   نُحَافِظُ عَلَى الْبِيئَةِ (nuhaafidhu ʿalaa l-bii'a) means: We look after the environment.

14. C — samaa'
   سَمَاءٌ is read samaa' and means sky.

15. A — bii
   The letter yaa after a kasra makes the vowel long, so بِي is bii.

16. A — ni
   نِ is read ni.

17. D — taa
   The letter ت is called taa.

18. C — akh
   أَخٌ is read akh and means brother.

19. D — laa
   لَا is read laa.

20. D — al-ahad
   al-ahad, Sunday, is the first day.

21. D — How fast or slow you read
   Pace is the speed of reading.

22. B — رَقْصٌ
   رَقْصٌ (raqs) means dance.

23. A — hadiyya
   هَدِيَّةٌ is read hadiyya and means gift.

24. A — بُرْتُقَالٌ
   بُرْتُقَالٌ (burtuqaal) means oranges.

25. C — خُضَارٌ
   خُضَارٌ (khudaar) means vegetables.

26. A — ghaym
   ghaym means clouds.

27. D — الْكُرْسِيُّ عِنْدَ الْبَابِ
   الْكُرْسِيُّ عِنْدَ الْبَابِ (al-kursiyyu ʿinda l-baab) means: The chair is at the door.

28. B — j as in jug
   The letter ج makes the sound j as in jug.

29. A — خَالٌ
   خَالٌ (khaal) means mother's brother.

30. C — ukht (sister)
   أُخْتٌ is ukht, sister.

31. C — Easy to read
   Legible writing can be read easily by other people.

32. A — ladhiidh
   لَذِيذٌ is read ladhiidh and means delicious.

33. B — kursii (chair)
   kursii is masculine. The other words end in -a and are feminine.

34. D — Pictures can be understood by people who speak different languages
   A picture can carry a message without words.

35. C — شَرَابٌ
   شَرَابٌ (sharaab) means drink.

36. A — We dance.
   nahnu means we and narqusu means we dance.

37. D — Kufic
   Kufic is an old angular style used for decoration and old manuscripts.

38. B — The sound and the meaning
   The Arabic word is on the front. The back has the sound and the meaning.

39. C — نَظِيفٌ
   نَظِيفٌ (nadhiif) means clean.

40. D — عِنْدَ
   عِنْدَ (ʿinda) means at (near, by).

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Today is Thursday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a group; share the lines and actions; stand facing the audience; say the poem together with actions; bow at the end.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example ghurfa (room), matbakh (kitchen), hammaam (bathroom), hadiiqa (garden).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning, up to 3.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: ab (father), umm (mother), akh (brother), ukht (sister), ibn (son), bint (daughter).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning, up to 4.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: The juice is cold.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: I clean my teeth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Opening: greet and say who you are. Middle: give the information. Closing: thank the audience.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: The friends will sing and eat the cake, because the cake has a candle and they stand round the table.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a sensible prediction and 1 mark for a reason from the picture.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Listen to the teacher and repeat; say the days in a chain; practise the sounds th and kh slowly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid method.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Everyone writes the same words for the same time; judges look at shape, size, spacing and neatness; everyone is encouraged and praised.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible rule.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: My hand is small.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Greeting customs can differ. Using polite words and a smile shows respect. Respect helps boys and girls, men and women to be treated equally and to live peacefully.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for customs differ, 1 mark for polite words, 1 mark for equality or peace.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: A small change in a sound can change the meaning, and careful copying makes you clear to the listener.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for change of meaning and 1 mark for being understood.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Look at the speaker; do not talk while someone is speaking; think about the topic; listen for words you know; ask a question at the end.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid behaviour, up to 3.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: This is my room.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw the item, colour it, write its Arabic name under it from right to left, write the meaning and check the spelling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: I like food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: The picture shows the meaning and writing the label practises the spelling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: I eat rice.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

60. (4 marks)
   Answer: mar-ha-ban (hello) and shuk-ran (thank you).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reading and 1 mark for each meaning.

61. (4 marks)
   Answer: shams (sun), sahaab (clouds), riih (wind), matar (rain).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.

62. (3 marks)
   Answer: Cut cards; write the Arabic day on the front; write the English name and sound on the back; decorate and display in order.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.
